title: customer-theta-incident-timeline-draft-noah-thompson
content:
PURPOSE:
- Internal scratchpad for Customer Theta (ThetaApps) production outage on 2026-02-24 -> 2026-02-25. Draft for timeline + internal comms. Keep rough — will refine for formal postmortem.

SUMMARY (high level):
- 2026-02-24 22:07 UTC: Customer reports elevated 5xx rates from hosted API (region eu-west-1).
- 22:10 UTC: CS triage, escalated to on-call SRE and serving-runtime.
- 22:18 UTC: Observability shows spike in model fallback errors and increased latency for route /theta/summarize.
- 22:35 UTC: Mitigation: route throttled (rate-limit lowered) + automatic fallback disabled to prevent cascading failures.
- 23:05 UTC: Traffic ramped down; error rate drop but intermittent 502s persisted until 2026-02-25 01:12 UTC.

COMMANDS / WHAT I RAN (logs + quick reproduction attempts):
- Pulled logs for the customer route:
  rcli logs --org thetaapps --route /summarize --start 2026-02-24T21:50Z --end 2026-02-25T01:30Z > theta-logs-0224.txt
- Grepped for 5xx errors and kernel OOMs:
  grep -E "5[0-9]{2}|CUDA out of memory|oom|kv cache" theta-logs-0224.txt | head -n 200
- Checked serving runtime health endpoints for affected pool:
  curl -sS http://10.45.3.12:8080/health | jq .
  -> returned {"status":"degraded","active_workers":"0/8"}  (note: some workers cycling)
- Tried a controlled request locally (dev environment) to reproduce:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"model":"rw-small-1", "input":"summarize: ..."}'
  -> reproduces latency ~1.2s in dev, but production spikes were 3-12s.

ERROR SNIPPETS (raw from logs):
- 2026-02-24T22:13:01Z [pool-a] WARN runtime: KV cache miss for model rw-large-2, seq_len=2048
- 2026-02-24T22:13:03Z [pool-a] ERROR runtime: model-inference-failure: CUDA out of memory while allocating 2.1GiB (requested by kernel 'matmul_fwd')
- 2026-02-24T22:13:03Z [pool-a] ERROR router: fallback-triggered: no compatible capacity for rw-large-2 in eu-west-1
- 2026-02-24T22:13:07Z [edge] ERROR proxy: upstream returned 502 Bad Gateway for request id=th-9a1f
- 2026-02-24T22:40:12Z [autoscaler] INFO scaler: added 2 nodes to pool-a (provision_delay=55s)

HYPOTHESES (initial):
1) Memory fragmentation or a sudden spike in seq_len causing OOMs in the rw-large-2 pool -> fallback attempts overloaded other pools -> cascading 502s.
2) Autoscaler lag: provisioning delay meant fallback requests queued against overloaded nodes leading to proxy timeouts.
3) A model variant/config change (recent release on 2026-02-23) introduced a kernel that increases peak memory usage for certain prompt patterns.

EVIDENCE SUPPORTING HYPOTHESES:
- OOM logs around the same timestamp as first error spike (supports hypothesis 1).
- Autoscaler added nodes ~27 minutes after first spike; during that window, active_workers reported low available workers (supports hypothesis 2).
- Linked PR (see linked_artifacts) for rw-large-2 quantization change merged 2026-02-23 (needs verification whether deployed to eu-west-1) (supports hypothesis 3).

TEMP MITIGATIONS WE TOOK / SUGGESTED:
- Immediate: Reduced concurrency for route /theta/summarize to 8r/s for customer-theta while we diagnose.
- Disabled automatic model fallback to avoid overloading smaller pools (observed cascade effect).
- Manually triggered addition of 4 reserved nodes to pool-a as hotfix (worked; error rate dropped).
- Medium-term: pin customer to rw-medium-1 for stable latency while we root cause rw-large-2 behavior.

TIMELINE (detailed):
- 2026-02-24 22:07 UTC: Customer reports Slack thread -> api errors (attachments with curl outputs).
- 22:10: On-call CS (I) triage; forwarded to SRE + serving-runtime with log snippets.
- 22:13: Serving-runtime reports repeated CUDA OOMs for rw-large-2 on pool-a (eu-west-1).
- 22:18: Router logs show multiple fallback attempts; proxy 502 spikes start at 22:19.
- 22:35: We rate-limited the route and disabled fallback — immediate drop in 502s but still occasional spikes.
- 22:40: Autoscaler triggers provisioning (2 nodes), delay ~55s to be ready.
- 23:05: Error rate down to baseline but intermittent 502s until 01:12; manual node add completed at 00:50 and stabilized traffic.
- 2026-02-25 09:00: Post-incident sync scheduled (owners: Ivy, SRE lead, runtime lead).

OPEN ACTIONS (owner / priority):
- [P0] serving-runtime: reproduce in staging with same prompt pattern and memory tracing (owner: Maya) -> due 2026-03-03
- [P0] infra: trace provisioning metrics and reduce cold-start/provision delay for pool autoscaler (owner: SRE) -> due 2026-03-10
- [P1] product: review recent model quantization PRs for rw-large-2 and rollback if flagged (owner: Model Onboarding) -> due 2026-03-05
- [P1] cs: finalize customer communication acknowledging outage + mitigation steps + ETA for stable pin (owner: Noah) -> draft by 2026-03-03

DRAFT INTERNAL BLURB (for #cs and #oncall summaries):
- Short: Customer Theta experienced elevated 5xx rates on 2026-02-24 caused by CUDA OOMs in the rw-large-2 serving pool (eu-west-1). Autoscaler provisioning lag and fallback cascades amplified the impact. Immediate mitigations (rate-limit, disabled fallback, added nodes) restored service. Postmortem in progress; next sync 2026-02-25 09:00 UTC.

DRAFT CUSTOMER-FACING NOTE (short):
- We saw intermittent errors on 2026-02-24 impacting summary requests. Root cause appears to be runtime memory pressure on the large model variant in eu-west-1 which caused fallback behavior and temporary timeouts. We have applied mitigations (reduced concurrency, added capacity, pinned to a stable model) and are investigating a permanent fix. We will follow up with a postmortem and timeline. (Will finalize once serving-runtime confirms root cause).

NOTES / THINGS TO CHECK (reminders):
- Confirm whether rw-large-2 quantization/PR on 2026-02-23 was deployed to eu-west-1 (deploy history).
- Get full HOOK traces for the OOM events (kernel, allocation stack).
- Check customer prompt distribution during the window for long-context or unusually high token counts.
- Validate whether rate-limiting earlier would have prevented fallback cascade (simulate).

PERSONAL NOTES (scratch):
- Keep this doc messy. Convert into proper timeline + RCA after Maya and SRE confirm repro.
- When preparing customer note, be explicit about what we changed and what we will do (pin, monitoring alerting thresholds, autoscaler improvements).
- Follow up with On-Call to add an alert for consecutive fallback-triggered events (threshold: 3 within 5m)

END OF DRAFT
